source_name: FloodGuard planning assessment overlay fixture (invented case, not a place)

case.title_th: กรณีทดสอบ 01 (ข้อมูลทดสอบ ไม่ใช่สถานที่จริง)
case.frame: Fifteen invented units and six engine rows (fixture, not a place)
case.fixture_notice: Fixture, not a place: every unit, input, date and number in this file is invented to exercise the parsers and the screens. Nothing here describes a real tambon, flood or detector.

scoring_frame.normalisation_rule: Absolute, declared anchors. No batch scaling and no max-normalisation (guardrail 2).
scoring_frame.flood_anchor_disclosure: The 0.20 anchor was declared after the 0.05 anchor was seen to saturate in 6 of the 8 Mae Sai tambons. It was chosen after seeing the data. Plan 3.4 says 5 of 8; the per-tambon envelope shares kept from that analysis show 6 above 0.05, and the owners corrected the count at signing on 2026-10-02.
scoring_frame.lane_disclosure: One flood input drives 4 of 5 components (90% of weight). This sentence appears on the overlay and in the brief appendix.

inputs.name: Fixture agency extent A (invented, not a product)
Fixture agency extent B, late date (invented, not a product)
Fixture own candidate (invented, not a detector)
Fixture season layer (invented, not a product)
Fixture layer kept local (invented, local level)

assumptions: Fixture, not a place: every unit, flood input, date and number is invented. The dates are in 2030.
The component and confidence records were produced by floodguard.normalisation and floodguard.confidence under the two signed protocol files, from the invented inputs each record echoes.
An invented input has no file: its sha256 is the SHA-256 of a fixture label.
The source timestamp of the fixture is the time it was written, because its inputs have no source.
The v2 results are laid out from invented trigger inputs by the evaluation order of protocol v1a. They show the shape of the secondary axis and are not the output of the v2 wrapper.
The headline-stability values are invented: no ensemble has run.
Planning guidance only. Not an official warning. Class E never means safe.
